title: A Wave That Connects
text: “Well, best to recover the kill right away and pull out, don’t you think? Best not to wander too close to civilization — we are wanted men, after all.”
“Agreed. Though we should still confirm there are no monsters we’ve missed.”
“Let’s go to the village~”

With that, Kou — carrying Itsuki — and Rabbit Guy went off to scout out the old woman’s village. Anyway, I made short work of the wave. While Yuki-chan and the others continued their race, I set about securing materials. And just as I was doing that…
“Hm?”
“Motoyasu-sama!”
Yuki-chan and the others came dashing over to me in a hurry. Whatever was the matter?
“I can smell a dragon.”
“What!?”

Could it be that, despite dispatching it at such blinding speed, Rival was lurking nearby after all? As I glanced warily around, Rafumi — disguised as Ren — approached slowly alongside Ren’s companions.
“What’s wrong? I thought you’d be fooling around forever, yet here you are, on high alert.”
“Yuki-chan and the others caught the scent of a dragon. Rafumi, surely you sense something too?”
“I haven’t exactly been scanning with that kind of certainty, but… hm. It seems Kuro senses something as well.”
“Mmm… the scent of a fated nemesis’s distant scheme is guiding Kuro and the others toward yet another battle of destiny—”
And just then, slowly descending from the sky… came that creature. Its form may have changed, but I knew it at once. Rival was here!
“You went and did it again, nano! Sending someone off to the other world this time — that’s a whole new level of screwing up, nano!”
Rival glared at me with a face full of fury, eyes brimming with hostility.
“Impossible!? How did it endure our furious onslaught!”
If I meant to finish it off, first I had to understand its methods! With all the Filolial-samas crying “Kweh!” in unison, threatening Rival, I pressed it for answers.
“You’re the idiot, nano! Just staking out this one wave was never gonna stop Gaelion from coming back, nano! There are other waves connected to that world too, nano!”
“Wh— what did you say!?”
From that answer alone, I could deduce the truth. It seemed there were waves in other nations connected to that other world. But once I knew that much, the next move would be simple enough.
“Try that again and Gaelion’s got plans of its own, so remember that, nano!”
“I refuse to remember any such thing!”
“I suppose it came here simply because this was a convenient rendezvous point.”
Rafumi, disguised as Ren, asked Rival. Rival turned to face her, blinked a few times, then nodded.
“That’s right, nano. And if you’re here as the backup measure that person prepared, then the whole thing with Filo must’ve gone off without a hitch, nano.”
“Correct.”
“So? Why’s Rafumi disguised as Sword Hero, nano?”
“That’s… not something I’ll be telling you, cha~n!”
To Rival’s question, Rafumi gave her usual reply.
“Oh, is that so, nano.”
“What a dull reaction. Ask more.”
“Is there even… any need to ask, nano? Seems like something you can figure out just by looking, nano.”
At Rival’s reply, Rafumi let out a deep sigh.
“How dull…”
“That’s my line, nano.”
“Rival, stay back!”
“Gaelion’s already got a lock on all of you this time around, so no matter where you go, your location can be pinpointed, nano.”
Damn it… was it saying that the moment we crossed paths, it was already game over!? In that case, silencing it here and now was the smart move! I gripped my spear tightly.
“Spear Hero? If you think Gaelion’s an easy kill here, you’re dead wrong, nano. You actually think this is Gaelion’s real body, nano?”
“Now you’re spouting nonsense just like Rafumi!?”
“Gaelion’s already a master of magic, nano. Don’t underestimate the Dragon Emperor, nano.”
Curse it… just how troublesome a monster had this thing grown into! Still, I was furious, so — Brionac! I drove it clean through, but the creature dissolved like mist and vanished from sight.
“Now, calm down, Spear Hero. Once you’ve been found out, there’s nothing to be done about it. Best to just deal with it honestly, don’t you think?”
“No thanks! My grudge remains unsettled. This loop’s peace is under threat!”
I bellowed at the top of my lungs.
“Rival! Go make peace with that other world of yours or something!”
“That world’s troublesome eyes have mostly been dealt with — Gaelion’s subordinates over there are handling the cleanup, so no problem, nano.”
…Curse it!

“Well, whatever — Gaelion’s done plenty of asking around before catching up with you, so it’s got a decent grasp of things, nano. Seems like this time around it went a lot like the loop when Gaelion first met you… running a circus, was it, nano?”
So it had already done its research and was catching up with us fully informed.
“Somehow Sword Hero’s gotten pretty famous… Rafumi, was that your doing, nano?”
“More or less, that’s correct.”
“Hey! Why are you explaining things so honestly!”
What was the meaning of Rafumi, who’d do anything so long as it amused her, talking so plainly with Rival? Just stay quiet!

“Hmph, Spear Hero. Don’t you understand? Keeping quiet only gets you answers that are obvious at a glance anyway. And what’s more, if we keep clashing carelessly with this one, even if things go fine in this world, the resulting grudge could hamper our mission once we move on to other loops.”
So Rafumi spouted on about how outright hostility was best avoided.
“What are you even talking about? I’ve already factored all that in — just go ahead and have your little spark-flying skirmishes with Rival every loop!”
Meanwhile, Filo-tan, Father, and I would get along splendidly.
“What a pain.”
“What a pain, nano.”
Why were the two of them giving the exact same reply there!? Grrgh… a pair of parasites mooching off my loop.
“Anyway, Spear Hero, it’s about time you gave some thought to how you’re going to handle yourself. After all, this one’s made its return.”

Rafumi replied as though she hadn’t the faintest idea what he meant. Thinking it over… was he talking about how things worked fine with Rafumi around, but not so well with Rival? …There was a high chance it would expose who’d turned Itsuki and Ren into fairy-shaped usaunnies!
“Gaelion figures you’ve been up to something dumb anyway, nano. Gaelion likes to think it’s pretty understanding, nano.”
“But being too understanding, too optimal, strips away all the fun and flexibility.”
“Gaelion plans to let things slide up to the point it can’t back down from, nano. Well… there are limits though, nano.”
“I don’t need your help! Get in my way and I won’t hold back!”
“Depends what you’ve been up to, nano.”
Grr… there were far too many things I couldn’t let Rival find out about, and it was troubling me.
“Dragons are the enemy.”
“Quite right. But Yuki-chan, this one is a far more troublesome monster than your average dragon. Attacking carelessly would be dangerous.”
“Say whatever you like, nano. Well… Gaelion’ll watch a bit longer and pick a good moment to join in, nano. Hey, Rafumi, help out with catching up, nano.”
“Fufufu… very well, I suppose I’ll lend a hand.”
“That was awfully agreeable, nano. There’s definitely something behind that, nano.”
“Don’t you dare lend a hand!”
That Rafumi truly never did anything decent. There was no way I could let Rival anywhere near Father, and yet here things were, growing more troublesome by the second.
“By the way, Rafumi, Big Sis and the others weren’t in the nest, nano. You know why, nano?”
“Ah, there’s a bit of a story there — they were entrusted elsewhere. Lured in by the circus atmosphere, they came wandering along without a care.”
“Huh… I see, nano.”
“Fufufu… you’ll see something quite amusing. By all means, go pay your sister a visit.”
“Something about making you happy feels wrong somehow, nano.”
And so… by the time Itsuki and the others returned, Rival had already slipped away without a trace. Just what was it plotting!
“Kou-san mentioned sensing a dragon’s presence somewhere.”
Itsuki and Rabbit Guy glanced warily around.
“Seems there was nothing left uncleared… let’s gather up the supplies and monster corpses and head back. It’d be a hassle if the kingdom’s people sniffed us out.”
“Indeed. Make sure to secure the boss’s corpse too.”

I hadn’t managed to prevent Rival from showing up, but I had secured the materials needed to raise Fleon-chan. And so, by showing off Yuki-chan and the others to Sage, I was able to finish registering the egg he’d given me — the one from which Fleon-chan would hatch. Though, given the state of affairs in the country, Sage had been somewhat wary. It was all a misunderstanding, though, and Sage came around once he saw my passion for Filolial-sama. And so… I was able to rejoin Father and the others, who’d taken refuge in Zeltoble and Siltvelt.
